standfirst: Gill-associated virus and yellow head virus, the shrimp roniviruses — invertebrate nidoviruses with a gene order found nowhere else in the order: the nucleoprotein gene sits upstream of the glycoprotein gene, and there is no discrete M gene. Nine features, including three cleavage products of one precursor and an 86 aa protein in an overlapping reading frame that no database holds.

modules.Okavirus: ORF1a and ORF1b joined by a −1 ribosomal frameshift at 23–25% efficiency; ORF2 encoding the 144–146 aa p20 nucleocapsid; ORF3 encoding a 1640–1666 aa precursor cleaved into p25 + gp116 + gp64; ORFX overlapping the 5' end of ORF3; and, in GAV only, an 83 aa ORF4.

gaps: No mature peptides are declared for the replicase. The ICTV profile states that the number and composition of the nsps released from pp1ab “is not yet known”. The dump does hold deposits annotated 3C-like protease (335–343 aa), helicase (660–846 aa) and RNA polymerase (92–286 aa), but these are domain fragments with no published junctions; only the 3CLpro specificity VxHE↓(L/V) is characterised (PMID 12502857), and a specificity is not a coordinate. They are bound to NOT_MODELLED as a deliberate decision. ORF1b deposits are likewise not modelled: ORF1b is never translated on its own, being reached only through the frameshift.
derived: The three ORF3 products are derived by cutting the precursor at two measured sites, not binned from deposits — the deposits named gp116 and gp64 are 267–338 aa fragments of a true 899 aa and 539 aa protein. PMID 12655087 placed the cuts between Ala228/Thr229 and Ala1127/Leu1128 of the 1666 aa precursor, and both verify exactly against every 1666 aa deposit here: ...LCFFITPAFA | TILSGI... and ...SIISPASA | LAPRQ..., each an [Ala-X-Ala] signal-peptidase-type-1 motif with the cut after the second Ala. The cut is made on the motif, never on the residue number: a 162 nt indel in ORF3 separates the YHV subtypes, so the second site sits at 1101 in GAV, 1117 in YHV-8 and 1127 in YHV-1. Over nine precursors, p25 came out at exactly 228 aa in all nine and the three products tile the precursor with a sum-minus-precursor of zero.

why.PX: 86 aa, from ORFX, an alternative frame overlapping the 5' end of ORF3 (PMID 20017924). Zero deposits — extracted from the genomes. In the process a published coordinate was corrected: the ICTV profile states ORFX “commences 3 nucleotides downstream of the pp3 initiation codon”, but a +3 nt offset is the same reading frame as pp3 and cannot encode a different protein. Measured directly in all three reference genomes the start is +5 nt, in the +2 frame, giving exactly 86 aa in every one; 15 extractions across the genus are all exactly 86 aa.
why.ORF4: 83 aa and GAV only — the corresponding yellow head virus ORF is truncated by a stop after 20 codons. Its size was settled by measurement: the ICTV profile gives 98 aa and the Walker & Sittidilokratna review gives 83 aa, and both GAV deposits here are 83 aa. It carries no copy_num, because marking a genus-partial protein essential would flag every yellow head virus genome.
why.P25: The N-terminal product, 228 aa in all nine precursors cut, carrying three transmembrane domains. The ICTV profile records no clear evidence of its association with virions and its function is unknown. Note the source disagreement, recorded rather than resolved: ICTV calls it p25 and the 2008 review calls it p22, both at 228 aa.
